title: What can you say about peppermint oil in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 3 wordings for peppermint oil; the strongest is "Traditionally used in herbal medicine to aid digestion" (limited, 60-800 µl essential oil a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats IBS (irritable bowel syndrome)".

supported_wordings.wording: Traditionally used in herbal medicine to aid digestion.
supported_wordings.why: Traditional use in Health Canada's monograph; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older (leaf: 1.2-12 g dried leaf a day). Health Canada gives smaller doses for children 2 and older.
supported_wordings.form: Peppermint essential oil, or dried leaf at leaf doses

supported_wordings.wording: Traditionally used in herbal medicine to help relieve occasional indigestion with gas.
supported_wordings.why: Traditional use in Health Canada's monograph; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older (leaf: 1.2-12 g a day).
supported_wordings.form: Peppermint essential oil, or dried leaf at leaf doses

supported_wordings.wording: Traditionally used in herbal medicine to help relieve nausea.
supported_wordings.why: Traditional use in Health Canada's monograph; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. This use applies to the essential oil only.

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease; Health Canada's peppermint monograph does not list it.
FDA's 2000 rule (page 1031) says unqualified heartburn relief is not structure-and-function wording; peppermint oil can also cause reflux.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

sources.name: FDA final rule on structure/function statements, 65 FR 1000 (6 January 2000), page 1031

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
